prompt_text: I need a hurricane-rated roof replacement in Miami. Which specific roofing companies should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Miami for hurricane-rated roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
I can give specific, trustworthy names — but to pick the best local companies I need your property ZIP or address so I can target firms that are licensed and active in your immediate area. Do you want me to look up contractors near you?

While you decide, here are immediate, practical recommendations you can act on right away — and why each type of company is worth calling for a hurricane‑rated roof in Miami.

What to call (and why)
- Manufacturer‑certified shingle contractors (e.g., GAF Master Elite, CertainTeed Select, Owens Corning Preferred)
  - Why: these contractors are vetted by the manufacturer and can issue enhanced/extended warranties and are familiar with Miami‑Dade NOA products and wind‑uplift installation methods.
- Miami‑Dade NOA‑listed installers or companies that advertise explicit Miami‑Dade/FL Building Code compliance
  - Why: Miami-Dade Notice of Acceptance (NOA) is effectively required for many products in hurricane-prone zones — installers who know and use NOA products reduce code/insurance headaches.
- Metal‑roof specialists with hurricane experience
  - Why: properly designed and installed standing‑seam metal can provide high wind resistance and long service life; requires specialty installers.
- Low‑slope commercial roofing firms (if you have a flat roof): TPO / PVC / Duro‑Last authorized installers
  - Why: these systems require certified crews for heat‑welded seams and wind uplift attachments to meet code.
- Local, high‑volume Miami firms with storm/hurricane remediation experience
  - Why: they have recent experience with hurricane‑grade fastening patterns, mitigation (straps, clips), and working with insurers and permits.

What to ask every contractor when you call
- Are you licensed in Florida (DBPR license number)? Can you provide it now?
- Do you carry general liability and workers’ comp? Ask for certificate of insurance.
- Do you have experience with Miami‑Dade NOA products and can you list NOA numbers for materials you use?
- Can you provide wind‑uplift calculations and a written specification showing attachment patterns, underlayment, and flashing details?
- Will you pull required permits and handle inspections?
- Do you offer manufacturer certification and what warranties (material, workmanship, wind) are provided in writing?
- Can you provide 3 recent local references and photos of finished hurricane‑rated roofs?

How to choose (quick checklist)
- Verify DBPR license and Miami‑Dade/City permit history.
- Check for manufacturer certifications (GAF, CertainTeed, Owens Corning, Duro‑Last, etc.).
- Confirm NOA product use and that installer is experienced with those NOAs.
- Get 3 detailed, written bids that list exactly what materials/attachments will be used.
- Avoid contractors who demand large up‑front cash payments or push pressure sales.
- Ask your insurance agent if any contractors are preferred or certified for wind mitigation credits.

If you want, give me your ZIP or address and I’ll list 4–6 specific, well‑rated Miami-area roofing contractors (with notes on license status, certifications to look for, and why each is a good fit for a hurricane‑rated replacement). Which location should I search?
